overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the non-reappointment vote was made in open session, and the later home visit and contacts with staff or counsel were not deliberation by a quorum. The AG also reminded the Board about notice specificity.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a quorum of selectmen privately decided, before the June 13, 2011 open meeting, not to reappoint a town employee and discussed a fire chief letter.
allegations.key_passage: we have not been presented with any evidence supporting this allegation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the board discussed the non-reappointment with town counsel and staff outside an open meeting, including individual follow-up calls on department recommendations.
allegations.key_passage: none of these discussions involved communication between a quorum of the Board.

allegations.summary: Two members went to the employee's home after the meeting to collect keys and deliver a separation letter; complaint said the decision to do so was made earlier.
allegations.key_passage: Their decision to collect the keys and deliver the agreement that night was not deliberation, since it involved only the administrative execution of a decision made during the earlier open meeting

allegations.summary: The June 13 notice listed only 'Appointments' as a topic; the AG commented that it lacked sufficient specificity, though no violation was found.
allegations.key_passage: The Board should have included more information about the specific "Appointments" the Board anticipated reviewing

allegations.summary: Complaint inferred that a cancelled May 31 executive session on personnel matters was intended to address the employee's non-reappointment.
allegations.key_passage: We are satisfied that this scheduled executive session was unrelated to Mr. Wheeler.
